title: System Design for the AI Era - Episode 1
content: The initial thought might be that users send prompts to an AI model, which responds. However, considering deeply, millions of users could send prompts simultaneously, necessitating infrastructure capable of handling such traffic. Users expect their conversations to be saved, thus requiring persistent storage. Users might upload files, necessitating file storage and processing. The AI may need to search information, so retrieval or tools are required. Users expect streaming responses instead of waiting for the entire answer, leading to the need for streaming infrastructure. Different requests may use different models, requiring model routing. Authentication, rate limiting, billing, logging, monitoring, safety systems, and failure recovery are also needed. Suddenly, the AI model is just one component within a much larger system. This is the mindset I want you to develop throughout this series. Whenever designing a system, start asking questions: How many users do.
